ef7daed03d1bd396e5571145524f4f6b5aa48f78: Small-scale resort, Molines-en-Queyras focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 35 km of runs are perfect for a 3 to 4 day stay, especially for families or skiers who don't need to constantly renew their playground. Molines-en-Queyras has kept the authentic identity of a mountain village, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. Here, people come for the clean air, the unspoilt landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. With a summit at 2830 m and a village at 1740 m, snow cover at Molines-en-Queyras is generally reliable from January to late March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause tension early in the season, but the situation recovers quickly with the first substantial snowfalls. At 40€, the day pass places Molines-en-Queyras in the mid-range category for budget: neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies the price for most skiers. In short: Molines-en-Queyras doesn't compete with the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

efa50ffaf2dfdde9c742f5ed773c9daef9d564c5: Corno del Renon is a low-key resort on a modest scale — 13 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. The family reputation of Corno del Renon is well earned: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a good-natured atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Northern Alps for laying the foundations of skiing with children. The altitude of Corno del Renon (1538 m at the base, 2260 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow reliability in mid-winter. January and February are the most dependable; in December and March, it's best to check conditions before finalising a booking. The day lift pass at 44€ places Corno del Renon in the mid-range category for budget — neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short: Corno del Renon doesn't rival the giants of skiing, and doesn't claim to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
